# Jubilees Chapter 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac's Weaning; Hagar and Ishmael Expelled; Mastema's Challenge

---

**17:1** In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee, Isaac was weaned. Abraham made a great feast in the third month on the day that his son Isaac was weaned.

**17:2** Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was present before his father Abraham, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed God because he had seen his sons and had not died childless.

**17:3** He remembered the words the LORD had spoken to him on the day Lot had separated from him, and he rejoiced because the LORD had given him seed upon the earth to inherit the earth. He blessed with all his heart the Creator of all things.

**17:4** Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael. She said to Abraham: "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac."

**17:5** The matter was very distressing to Abraham because of his servant's son.

**17:6** God said to Abraham: "Do not be distressed because of the boy or because of your slave woman. Listen to everything Sarah says to you, for through Isaac your descendants shall be named."

**17:7** "And also the son of the slave woman — I will make him into a nation, for he is your seed."

**17:8** Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, placed them on Hagar's shoulder, and sent her and the child away.

**17:9** She departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. When the water in the skin was spent, the child became thirsty; he could not walk and fell down under one of the trees.

**17:10** His mother picked him up and placed him under a tree; she went and sat down at a distance — about a bowshot away — for she said: "Let me not look on the death of the child."

**17:11** She sat and wept, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said: "What is wrong with you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is."

**17:12** "Rise, lift up the boy and hold him by your hand, for I will make him a great nation."

**17:13** God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water; she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink, and he revived.

**17:14** Ishmael grew, lived in the wilderness, and became an archer.

**17:15** God was with him, and his mother took for him a wife from Egypt.

**17:16** It came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth day of that month, that there were voices in heaven concerning Abraham — that he was faithful in all that God had told him, and that he loved the LORD, and that in every trial he remained faithful.

**17:17** The prince Mastema came and said before God: "Behold, Abraham loves his son Isaac and delights in him above all else. Command him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering on the altar, and you will see whether he will carry out this command; then you will know whether he is truly faithful in everything you test him with."

**17:18** The LORD knew that Abraham was faithful in all his trials; for he had tried him through his native land and through famine, and had tried him through the wealth of kings, and through his wife when she was taken from him, and through circumcision, and through Ishmael and Hagar his servant woman when he sent them away.

**17:19** And in everything in which he was tried, he was found faithful; his soul was not impatient and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the LORD.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. Mastema's accusation (v.17) as parallel to Job 1:6-12 preserved. The inventory of Abraham's prior trials (v.18) preserved in full. "Prince Mastema" title retained.*
